searchText: No need for a Micah checkbox, and I don't represent any client team. <@!758579010027782144> can represent Nethermind hi, not sure if it is correct channel for ether.js interactions via RPC api i want to use https://docs.ethers.io/v5/api/contract/contract/#Contract-on and listen to any event for any new incoming transactions on a given contract by subscribing over wss. does it detect both eip-1559 & non eip-1559 transactions? does it detect internal transactions ? is there any timeout or is it bound by rpc provider regarding for how i can keep wss connection open ? is it client agnostic ? thanks, i am not able to find answers to these anywhere <@!358385024573243393> <@!370231100850831380> I think the proper channel for asking ethers.js questions is https://github.com/ethers-io/ethers.js/discussions Also, tagging maintainers like that is generally considered rude apologies, will take care from now onwards Just to review we have Nethermind: <@758579010027782144> Geth: <@360491619402776577> Felix Lange (not sure about discord ID) Who will be representing openethereum, besu, and erigon? <@194432762315407360> ^ (Tldr. we're responsible for reviewing the json rpc api changes + edge cases) Is this about the tests? What do people think about automated testing (via hive) of the RPC? It seems to me this would be easier than having devs from each client sign off on the implementation of each method Then we can focus the discussions around deviations What is this for? Does it make sense to include someone from the Hardhat team? <@!130156954273316865> it's to approve the RPC definitions that <@!104006934562107392> and <@!181920051333431296> have been working on probably makes sense to include someone from hardhat if they have some time

excerpts.author: hack3r_0m
excerpts.content:
hi, not sure if it is correct channel for ether.js interactions via RPC api

i want to use https://docs.ethers.io/v5/api/contract/contract/#Contract-on and listen to any event for any new incoming transactions on a given contract by subscribing over wss.

does it detect both eip-1559 & non eip-1559 transactions?
does  it detect internal transactions ?
is there any timeout or is it bound by rpc provider regarding for how i can keep wss connection open ?
is it client agnostic ?

thanks, i am not able to find answers to these anywhere
